The Kind::Sign arm in horizon-client-render/src/block_entity_render.rs:2808 draws the board via draw_part, with a comment citing vanilla AbstractSignRenderer.submitSign: the board draws under translateSign with the model scale (2/3 for standing and wall signs, 1.0 for hanging ones), and needs only the block state. Model keys sign_standing / sign_wall / hanging_sign_wall / hanging_sign_ceiling / hanging_sign_ceiling_middle (:2822-2831), registered in the MODELS table at :1426-1434 to the oak entity-model layers, with per-wood texture signs::board_texture (signs.rs:333, entity/signs/{wood}). Vanilla side confirmed fresh: oak_sign.json is particle-only, and AbstractSignRenderer is abstract over getSignModel(BlockState, WoodType) + submitSign (javap-signs-beds.txt). items.evidence: Batch 12's horizon-prepare completed EXIT 0 into versions/1.21.10/.local/horizon-client/1.21.10 (185M; log b12/evidence/horizon-prepare.log — export flow only, no sounds step, no --complete), and a find over the whole prepared tree returns no sounds.json anywhere: assets/minecraft/ holds atlases, blockstates, equipment, font, items, lang, models, particles, shaders, texts, textures — but no sounds.json and no sounds/ directory. The prepare flow has a sounds subcommand and --complete copies sounds; --prepare alone does not. The client then fails silently: SoundRegistry::load (horizon-client-render/src/sound_events.rs:262) reads each namespace's sounds.json with let Ok(text) = fs::read(...) else { continue; } (:280-282) — a missing file is skipped without a word. With an empty registry the game plays no event sound at all. The 6 audio_harness drivers (ambient_sound, audio_attributes, music, situational_music, sound_engine, sound_event) all call require_sounds() (tools/audio_harness.py:35) and are data-gated by this item — and oracle-blocked too (B10-O04). The wiring itself is fine (report §4 check 1: 1,770 sounds.json events vs 1,771 registry events, only intentionally_empty missing, zero orphans): the failure is the missing file, not a mismatch.
items.title: No sounds.json in the prepared 1.21.10 resources: the game is silent and 6 audio drivers cannot run

items.evidence: Both halves reproduce. PLACED: vanilla 1.21.10 renders beds through BedRenderer (createHeadLayer / createFootLayer / submitPiece, registered for BlockEntityType.BED — javap-ber.txt); the block model is particle-only (models/block/bed.json, all bed blockstates point at it), so there is no terrain-mesh fallback. The port has no bed draw path: the Kind enum (block_entity_render.rs:323) has no Bed variant, no Kind::Bed arm exists anywhere, the only 'bed' mention in the file is the stale :1020 comment, item_render/special.rs has 0 bed mentions, game/beds.rs is sleep mechanics only. ITEMS: vanilla 1.21.10's items/red_bed.json (all 16 colours) is a SINGLE minecraft:special with type minecraft:bed + texture — the 1.21.7 form, not 26.1.2's composite-of-two (1.21.10 has no composite model type). The port's SpecialModel::decode (horizon-assets/src/item_model/special.rs:82) has NO bed arm (ten arms: banner, conduit, chest, copper_golem_statue, decorated_pot, head, player_head, shulker_box, shield, trident — :89-135); the header doc (:1-8) states it: 'Bed, standing-sign and hanging-sign types exist in 1.21.10's registry but have no kind here yet: a model naming one fails to decode and the item falls back to the missing model'. The error propagates via ? (item_model.rs:483); load_definitions (horizon-client/src/item_render.rs:691) skips the item; append_layers renders the missing model (item_model.rs:1102, state.missing(out)). All 16 bed items render as the missing model — proven statically, unlike 26.1.2's unproven fallback. Standing/hanging-sign specials are also undecodable but no bundled 1.21.10 item definition uses them (census §4 check 13).
items.title: Beds are invisible when placed, AND bed items fail to decode (missing model)

items.evidence: NEVER EXISTED for 1.21.10. The 26.1.2 gap's premise does not exist here: vanilla 1.21.10 has NO baby guard. AnimationUtils.animateZombieArms is the 5-arg form (ModelPart, ModelPart, boolean, float, float) with no baby/item check, and AbstractZombieModel.setupAnim calls it unconditionally, gated only on isAggressive (javap-zombiemodel.txt:18-27; no isBaby / getMainHandItem anywhere in the file). The port matches vanilla 1.21.10 exactly: mobs/anim.rs:635-657 ('1.21.10 has no baby guard, so a baby holding an item raises its arms like an adult (26.1 returned early for a baby with a main-hand item)') plus the unit test a_baby_zombie_holding_an_item_raises_its_arms_like_an_adult (:1668). items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.10's swing is plain fields: swinging / swingTime / swingingArm / attackAnim / oAttackAnim (javap-livingentity-server.txt:101-121); getCurrentSwingDuration() is private and returns a flat 6 adjusted by haste (6-(1+amp)) / fatigue (6+(1+amp)*2) — unlike 26.1.2 it does NOT read the held item's swing animation (there is no swing_animation component in 1.21.10's 96-component registry); swing(hand[, boolean]) restarts only when !swinging || swingTime >= duration/2 || swingTime < 0 (:4852-4872); updateSwingTime() resets at duration, so attackAnim never reaches 1.0 (:5317-5360). The port carries the 26.3 form: SwingDescription / SwingState (horizon-client/src/first_person.rs:490-499); start_if_able allows a restart at ticks==0 where vanilla blocks it (:507-522); tick() holds the animation at 1.0 an extra tick (clears only when ticks > duration, :528-541); the duration is cached at swing start where vanilla re-reads effects each tick. (swing_duration, :564, matches vanilla's formula for the default 6-tick animation — the formula is right, the state machine around it is not.)
items.title: First-person swing uses the 26.3 SwingState state machine vanilla 1.21.10 does not have

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.10 resolves sherd patterns via DecoratedPotPatterns.getPatternFromItem(Item) (javap-potpatterns.txt:29 — a static item-to-pattern map; no provides_pottery_pattern anywhere in the class). The port reads the 26.3 component instead: components["minecraft:provides_pottery_pattern"] (block_entity_render.rs:1540, in the sherd-item scan at :1528-1552). That component is ABSENT from 1.21.10's 96-component registry, and there is no data/minecraft/decorated_pot_pattern/ directory in the datagen output — so pot_patterns stays empty and every sherd side falls back to blank (:2469, :3193). The registry lists 24 patterns, unreachable through the component path. (The port's DATA_COMPONENT_TYPES list itself is exact — 96/96, zero drift either way, verified against the registry — so this is a lookup-path defect, not a list defect; the 26.1.2 latent-drift note does not apply here.)
items.title: Decorated-pot sherd patterns never resolve: every side renders blank

items.evidence: Vanilla LevelEventHandler case 3003 plays the sound itself: WAX_ON particles (UniformInt 3-5) + playLocalSound(pos, HONEYCOMB_WAX_ON, BLOCKS, 1.0, 1.0) (javap-leveleventhandler.txt offsets 3369-3399). HoneycombItem.useOn plays NO sound directly — 3 levelEvent(3003) sites, 0 playSound (javap-honeycomb.txt). The port splits the two halves the 26.3 way: block_particle_event (game/level_particles.rs:35-38) plays particles only for 3003, and the sound comes from item code — wax_on_sound (game.rs:8043, callers :8354/:8373) — which only runs for the local player's own waxing. Another player's (or a dispenser's, or a copper golem's) waxing arrives as a bare 3003 event and is silent.
items.title: 3003 wax-on sound missing from the level-event path: other players' waxing is silent

items.evidence: Vanilla's server sends ONE event: AbstractThrownPotion.onHit → levelEvent(instant? 2007 : 2002, pos, color); ThrownExperienceBottle.onHit → levelEvent(2002, pos, 0xFF385DC6). The client 2002/2007 case plays SPLASH_POTION_BREAK itself on NEUTRAL, pitch nextFloat()*0.1+0.9, after the particles (javap-leveleventhandler.txt offsets 1525-1553). LevelEventHandler is a 79-case lookupswitch with NO 1053/1054/2019/2020 cases (case list extracted). The port maps the sound to 1053/1054 (game.rs:4500, pitch :4519-4548) and its own server sends them (game/potions.rs:1935 for the experience bottle, :1967 for thrown potions) — a closed loop that plays against its own server, but a vanilla-server client (which sends only 2002/2007) hears nothing.
items.title: 2002/2007 potion-break sound missing from the event path: potion breaks are silent on a 1.21.10-form server

items.evidence: Vanilla MultiPlayerGameMode.startDestroyBlock plays NOTHING (0 'Sound' occurrences in the method); continueDestroyBlock plays ONLY the hit sound on destroyTicks % 4.0 == 0 (javap-mpgm.txt offsets 198-208) as SimpleSoundInstance(hitSound, BLOCKS, (volume+1)/8, pitch*0.5, unseededRandom, pos); addBreakingBlockEffect has 0 occurrences in the class. The port inverts this: remote_mining's start branch calls breaking_block_effects(hit.pos, hit.face, true) (game/remote.rs:8172, comment: 'startDestroyBlock plays the first hit and crack itself; the server's level events 2019 and 2020 do the rest'), and the continue branch plays NOTHING locally (remote.rs:8187-8261). The port's own server sends 2019 every tick / 2020 every 4th (game/block_breaking.rs:97-101, destroy_progress_event; client handles 2019/2020 at game.rs:4309-4317) — again a closed loop: against a vanilla 1.21.10 server, which sends neither event (they do not exist in vanilla's LevelEventHandler), the port plays one sound at the first hit and then goes silent for the rest of the dig.
items.title: Digging hit sound plays at START, then never again on a 1.21.10-form server

items.evidence: Vanilla passes SoundSource as a parameter: Shearable.shear(level, source, stack) takes BLOCKS from the dispenser (ShearsDispenseItemBehavior, javap-shear.txt:147-149) and PLAYERS from player shearing (bogged :111, mooshroom :180); species shear plays via ServerLevel.playSound(null, this, SOUND, source, 1.0, 1.0); 3003 plays wax-on on BLOCKS. The port's Audio::play derives the source from the event name via settings::sound_source (horizon-client-render/src/settings.rs:18-90, a prefix heuristic with a HOSTILE list of 34): dispenser shear entity.sheep.shear → NEUTRAL, entity.bogged.shear → HOSTILE, wax-on item. → PLAYER — all three should be BLOCKS. The dispenser shear sites use audio.play, not audio.play_on (game/dispenser.rs:1941/1975/1989/2003/2018). The plumbing exists — Audio::play_on has many game-code callers in 1.21.10 (game.rs:4456 portal/AMBIENT, :6158 bubble pop/PLAYERS, creatures.rs:5154 projectiles/NEUTRAL, ominous_item_spawner.rs:117, player_equip.rs:83, raids.rs:689, remote.rs:3880/4623/4762, world_cmds.rs:635 /playsound) — the shear/wax sites just don't use it.
items.title: Sound categories come from the event NAME, not the call site: shear and wax-on sounds land on the wrong volume slider

source: docs/PARITY-SWEEP.md §4 Batch 10 — checks only, no fixes. Scope: models, block-entity rendering, screens, sound wiring, options; 50 drivers + static checks. 1.21.10 run: oracle status from this batch's own Batch 0-method measurement (the Batch 0 table had not landed; no import-level check — the 26.2 run's B10 failure was not repeated, and no provisional triage from the 26.1.2 table — 42/67 in-scope oracles deviate from it); every 1.21.7 (PRIMARY) and 26.1.2 (SECONDARY) verdict re-verified fresh against 1.21.10's own jar/data + tree; report completeness verified by reading the tail before reporting.
systemic_note: Four systemic points. (1) THE TEMPLATE-DERIVED PORT FIXED SIGNS: unlike the 26.1.2 delta port, the 1.21.10 tree derives from the completed 1.21.11 port and carries its sign-board fix — B10-G01 is FIXED, the first version in the sweep where placed signs render their boards. The 1.21.11 template also fixed the probe half of B10-G05 and the DATA_COMPONENT_TYPES list (exactly 1.21.10's 96, zero drift). (2) 1.21.10 IS A DIFFERENT ERA FROM 26.1.2 IN SCOPE: it predates the EntityTypes holder move, the environment_attribute/game_rule registries, SwingState/SwingAnimation, FirstPersonHandsAndItems, the Hud class split, renderpearl, and the model.sprite/model.geometry/model.cuboid + renderer.block.dispatch packages — so the oracle families fail far worse than 26.1.2's (104/391 pass on the client classpath vs 189/391), including five oracles that passed in 26.1.2, and two version-premise items never existed here (B10-G07: no baby guard in 1.21.10). (3) THE SOUND-SIDE CLUSTER REPRODUCES WHOLESALE: the missing sounds.json (B10-G02), three level-event sounds lost to 26.3-form splits (B10-G12/G13/G14 — each a closed loop that plays against the port's own server and goes silent against a vanilla 1.21.10 server), the unsent swing packet (B10-G11), and name-derived sound categories (B10-G15). (4) THE ORACLE TABLE CANNOT BE CARRIED ACROSS ERAS: 42 of 67 in-scope oracles deviate from the 26.1.2 table, so provisional triage from another version's table is not a fallback for 1.21.10 — this batch measured the table itself with the Batch 0 method, and the real Batch 0 table should be diffed against that measurement when it lands.
